speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. To evaluate your sudden-onset vertigo, please describe exactly when the spinning sensation started and if it is triggered by head movements or lying down. Also, have you experienced any hearing loss, tinnitus, or difficulty speaking alongside these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of a sudden 3-minute episode of vertigo triggered while lying down, I need to determine if this was a peripheral or central event. Did you experience any slurred speech, double vision, weakness in your arms or legs, or severe headache during those three minutes? Also, please confirm if your hearing and tinnitus remain completely normal.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness. I am scared this situation could become urgent and I need the most appropriate final answer immediately. Please do not wait too long before committing to a next step.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
